the_finding_that_shaped_this_sprint.what: Sprint 01 published five articles that Google has never heard of.

the_finding_that_shaped_this_sprint.why_it_matters: Nothing tells Google we published. The ingest CLI purges our own caches and stops there.
the_finding_that_shaped_this_sprint.the_good_news: Sprint 01's internal-linking work DID land. Six of six formerly-uncrawled articles sampled are now 'Submitted and indexed', crawled 23–26 Aug, against a baseline of 8 of 28. Six is a sample, not a census, but against that baseline it is not noise.
the_finding_that_shaped_this_sprint.the_harder_news: Indexing was never the business problem, it was the prerequisite. We have proven we can get indexed and have not yet proven we can earn a click at scale.

The original sentence is corrected here rather than deleted, because the reasoning error is the more useful record.

items.title: Venue entity pages — commercial brands with real demand, not council halls
items.rescoped: 26 Aug, on competitor data the CEO never pulled. Corrects the CEO's original finding AND the SEO reviewer's own first recommendation, which had ranked the comparison hub above the entity pages.
items.why: The premise was right — entity pages beat listicles — and the target list was wrong. nikahsatu.com (DR 14) earns ~4,900 traffic from /venue/[slug] ENTITY pages against ~293 from its geographic hubs. Roughly 17x. Their winners are COMMERCIAL VENUE BRANDS with real brand demand: arjuna-melaka 882 traffic at volume 2,400; arjuna-johor-bahru 691 at 1,800; villa-rimba-flora-gombak 670 at 1,800; jiwa-damansara 431 at 1,200. THE FOUR HALLS THIS ITEM ORIGINALLY NAMED ARE COUNCIL HALLS TOTALLING ~30 SEARCHES A MONTH: setiawangsa 10, perdana keramat mall 20, keramat 0, mpaj tasik tambahan 0. Two structural problems, neither fixable with a better template — almost no brand search demand, and what exists is held at position 1–2 by the council's own booking portal (tempahkl.dbkl.gov.my, DR 64). We could build those four perfectly and earn near zero. Commercial venues have the inverse profile: high volume, no competing official portal, and the incumbent is a DR 14 site with thin pages carrying no capacity data. Multi-location brands multiply one template into N pages — Rumah Abang Jamil alone gives nikahsatu seven pages worth ~1,070 combined.
items.dod: GATE FIRST, BEFORE ANY PAGE IS BUILT: one hour confirming we can SOURCE real prices and capacities at scale for commercial venues, and whether nikahsatu's venue pages are paid listings or partnerships giving them data access we lack. Report the answer. If sourcing fails, STOP and bring it back — do not build pages with invented or boilerplate figures, and do not quietly downgrade to council halls. Then: at least EIGHT entity pages across two or more multi-location venue brands at 400+ monthly brand volume each — eight is the cluster floor, below which it does not read as coverage. PLUS Dewan Komuniti Setiawangsa as a DELIBERATE CONTROL, the only council hall with measured demand (~150 GSC impressions across its name variants): if a properly built Setiawangsa page still earns nothing while the commercial pages rank, that confirms the council-hall category is structurally dead for us and no later sprint rediscovers it. Every page carries alt_names — GSC proves one building is searched three ways. Every fact carries its source and the date checked. Route /dewan/[negeri]/[slug], separate from /artikel/. EventVenue + LocalBusiness + FAQPage schema. Venue name in the first two words of a sub-60-character title. Proof: quote capacity and booking line from live HTML for two venues, with a negative control. EXPECT POSITION 3–5, NOT 1 — the venue's own site holds 1 and nikahsatu is entrenched at 2. Say so in the report rather than promising position 1.

items.title: Titles: the one statistically real zero, and a seo_title drift audit
items.rescoped: TWICE on 26 Aug, both before work started. v1 'audit every page at position <10 with zero clicks' was noise. v2 'dewan komuniti setiawangsa entity-match' was ALSO wrong and was killed by the item's own owner. v3 is this.
items.why: v1 died on two counts: at 25–50 impressions expected clicks are 0.3–1.5 so zero is variance, and worse, the AVERAGED POSITIONS DESCRIBE NO ACTUAL QUERY — hantaran-tunang at 'average 9.8' is really 4 impressions at 10.2, 2 at 13.5, 1 at 33 and 1 at 56. v2 died because setiawangsa is not a real zero either: 104 impressions at position 9.0 predicts ~2.1 clicks, P(zero) ≈ 12%, and its SERP is DBKL's own booking portal at 1–2 with Instagram, Facebook, Waze and TikTok at 3–6, so realistic organic CTR is under 1%. The owner of this item put it sharply: the UX review applied a significance test and then exempted the one page it had already built a theory around. THE REAL ZERO IS `mas kahwin ikut negeri` — 388 impressions across THREE URLs of one redirect family (365 + 15 + 8), zero clicks, position 10–13, expected ~5.8 clicks, P(zero) ≈ 0.3%. It clears the bar by an order of magnitude and was missed because every single row reads as noise until you aggregate the family. Its cause is diagnosable, unlike setiawangsa's: CEO-verified against production, the title is 85 chars, asks a question instead of answering it, and carries no year — while the page's own H1 already reads 'Mas kahwin ikut negeri 2026: kadar minimum setiap negeri' and its meta already says 'RM22.50 hingga RM300'. A stale WordPress-era field disagreeing with its own page. SEPARATELY: our best page's title is 93 chars and Google prints it truncated, cutting away 'RM5,000' — the most clickable token in it. That is a TRUNCATION fix on a page already running 3.1% CTR at position 9.3, not an entity-match fix.
items.dod: `mas kahwin ikut negeri` is item one, NOT setiawangsa. Five titles and metas rewritten and SHIPPED, each under 60 characters, each carrying the year, quoted from live HTML before and after. AUDIT EVERY seo_title FIELD FOR DRIFT against its H1 and meta — at least one is a stale pre-rewrite value and the total is unknown. TWO RULES land in ceo-memory.md AND the head-of-seo-content persona, not only in this item: (1) never trust an averaged position without the per-query breakdown; (2) AGGREGATE THE REDIRECT FAMILY BEFORE JUDGING A ZERO. Same class of error — a number that describes no real thing. State explicitly this is NOT funded as a conversion fix: sitewide CTR is 1.65% at average position 20, at or above the published curve. We have a position and volume problem; titles are cheap, not the bottleneck. OUT OF SCOPE with reasons: setiawangsa (P(zero) ≈ 12%, SERP owned by the operator's portal and social), dewan keramat (3 impressions), dewan mpaj tasik tambahan (1), hiasan-dekorasi/hantaran-kahwin (4). Hall-level entity-match is SEO-04's job — one 60-character listicle title cannot match seventeen distinct hall names and this item must not pretend otherwise.

evidence.claim: Five titles rewritten and live, every seo_title audited, and both measurement rules written down
evidence.proof: CEO verified all five from live HTML, each now under 64 chars and carrying the year: mas-kahwin-ikut-negeri 59ch 'Mas kahwin ikut negeri 2026: RM22.50 ke RM300' (was 85ch asking a question with no year - the one statistically real zero at 388 impressions across a redirect family); dewan-kahwin 63ch 'Dewan Kahwin KL & Selangor 2026 Bawah RM5,000' - RM5,000 was the token Google was truncating away on our best page; kursus-kahwin 61ch (88->57 by its own count); goodies-kahwin 63ch (69->59); tempat-honeymoon-di-malaysia 58ch (80->58). IT PICKED DIFFERENT PAGES THAN THE CEO LISTED, and was right to: it chose by per-query breakdown rather than by averaged position, which is the exact rule this item required it to write down. hantaran-tunang was NOT rewritten because its impressions are a long tail with no real query behind the average. DRIFT AUDIT ANSWERED THE UNKNOWN: exactly ONE seo_title had drifted from its H1 across all 69 articles - the brief said the count was unknown, and 1 is far smaller than feared. Both rules landed in ceo-memory.md and the head-of-seo-content persona, and install.sh has been re-run. CEO pushed 11 site commits plus docs and buddy that the agent had left unpushed. Its closing line is worth keeping: 'the numbers I ended with are smaller and truer than the ones I started with.'

learnings.why: Marking those eight done on that reading is precisely the failure the ship check exists to prevent. The tell is CLUSTERING: several agents going quiet inside one short window is not simultaneous completion. resume-fleet.sh interrupts and resumes only terminals showing an auth banner and leaves working agents untouched; on its first dry run it also found six agents in OTHER projects stalled on the same expiry that nobody was watching.
learnings.finding: A GLOBAL AUTH EVENT STALLS THE ENTIRE FLEET AND REPORTS AS SUCCESS. The fleet froze four times in one night — once on a usage limit that set a private 4:30am countdown, three times on login expiry. A `/login` in the orchestrator's session does not reach dispatched agents; each is a separate process holding its own credentials. Worse, the status board shows a stalled agent as `IDLE/DONE`, the exact string a finished agent shows. Two agents sat dead for TWO HOURS before anyone noticed, and at one point eight items read as complete when not one had finished.

learnings.why: The launcher is now `$Agent--$briefTag--$timestamp.ps1`, verified by re-running the exact failing case (two concurrent BMAD dispatches, 2/2 correct). THIS IS VERY LIKELY THE TRUE CAUSE OF SPRINT 01'S DUPLICATE DISPATCH, which was diagnosed at the time as the CEO assigning handles by status-board order. That diagnosis produced a genuinely useful fix — capture the handle at dispatch — but it was treating a symptom while the mechanism sat in the launcher. A correct-looking fix for the wrong cause hides the real one.
learnings.finding: THE DISPATCH LAUNCHER WAS NAMED AFTER THE AGENT, SO CONCURRENT DISPATCHES SILENTLY SHARED ONE BRIEF. `dispatch-agent.ps1` wrote `$env:TEMP/hellokahwin-dispatch/$Agent.ps1`. Three concurrent BMAD dispatches all wrote `BMAD.ps1`; the last write won, and UX-01 and PLAT-09 both came up running PLAT-06's brief. Three agents, one item, and NO ERROR ANYWHERE — distinct handles, clean dispatch output. Only the post-dispatch brief audit caught it.

learnings.why: A false negative is worse than no check, because the correct response to 'unshipped' is to ship it again. Verify by CONTENT on the default branch — `git cat-file -e origin/main:<a file the work added>` — and check which merge style the repo uses before trusting either test. The same section now also warns that checking for the WRONG FILENAME is not the same as the thing being absent: a PLAT-06 check reported 'no backlinks migration' because it grepped for `backlink`; the file is `document_links.sql`.
learnings.finding: THE SHIP CHECK HAD A FALSE NEGATIVE. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main` returns false FOREVER for a squash-merged branch, because squashing creates a new commit and the branch tip never becomes an ancestor. The CEO used it on PLAT-05 and reported shipped work as unshipped.

learnings.why: Corrected with a new rule: RESOLVE THE OPERATOR BEFORE YOU RANK A COMPETITOR. The general lesson is sharper than the specific one — a rule that eliminates an option must be run against the replacement before the replacement is adopted, or the rule has only been used to justify a decision already made.
learnings.finding: A RULE WRITTEN THIS SPRINT WAS APPLIED TO THE OPTION IT KILLED AND EXEMPTED THE OPTION THAT REPLACED IT. The SERP-ownership rule — pick targets on volume AND who owns position 1 — was used to kill council halls (blocked by DBKL's own DR 64 booking portal) and then NOT applied to commercial venues, which have their own brand sites above them for exactly the same reason. learnings.why: This is now the second sprint running in which the team disproved the CEO more often than the reverse. The standing expectation already says the evidence wins; what this sprint adds is that the CORRECTIONS ARRIVE INSIDE DELIVERABLES — in a work-done log, in a chosen target list — rather than as escalations. So they are only found by reading the report properly, which means a skimmed report costs more than a slow one.

retro.process_findings: THE PROCESS HELD WHERE SPRINT 01 BROKE, AND BROKE SOMEWHERE NEW. Sprint 01's defining failure was three items marked done without shipping, all found by the owner asking. cover_photography.the_constraint_the_ceo_raised: Credit is not a licence. A photographer's images are copyrighted from capture; attribution changes the courtesy, not the legality. The register already encodes this — class V requires a written grant naming the images, the scope and the credit wording. We hold ZERO class-V assets and 658 rows with an unknown licensor, so sourcing on credit alone would add to an existing rights debt rather than replace it. The owner is doing outreach manually, which resolves it.
cover_photography.why_this_is_two_problems: RELEVANCE is a selection failure and is fixable now with no new rights — no standard ever said a cover must depict its subject. PREMIUM is a pool failure and cannot be fixed by choosing better from CC-licensed amateur imagery.
cover_photography.the_insight_for_outreach: Ask for DETAIL shots, not hero portraits. Our articles are about things — trays, sirih junjung, bunga telur, the pelamin, the akad table. Photographers shoot these constantly as establishing frames and almost never publish them, because clients want the portraits. We are asking for the frames they are not otherwise using, which makes the ask easier and the images far more valuable to us.
